verdict:
Better than r1, but not at fern's level yet. Mean 5.5. The two worst r1 problems are mostly fixed. Pack is no longer mud: 22.6% of graded pixels are below L20 (Rec.709 luma), against 53% before. The overheads now fall off from the lamp: the duvet is about L150 by the lamp and about L60 at the foot. In window, Dawn is larger and near the right third, and her head (about L40-50) is brighter than the sky behind it (about L31). Accept is a good new establishing frame: a diagonal bed, a lamp island and a clear subject. Overhead_pre states the 'luggage full' idea plainly: one closed case and three gifts, with no extra bag yet.

What still makes it look amateur:
(1) The hands. In pack, the gripping hand is a white plaster fist (about L90 against a sleeve of L25) with no fingers you can read. In accept, the screen-right hand (about L160) is as bright as her face (about L147) and reads as a white glove. In overhead_pre, the right hand stops splayed against the side of the case instead of resting on it. Seen from straight above, the left hand reads as sitting on her own shoulder.
(2) Pack does not show 'into'. The camera sees the duffel's closed top. The eased mouth is on the duffel's -Y side (BAG turn 180): it faces Dawn and is edge-on to this camera. The burgundy bag hangs down the outside of the duffel, so it reads as hanging beside the duffel, not going into it.
(3) Continuity. The open case in overhead reads as a rigid hard shell: a thin, even, black rounded rim (the cut wall with the black zip tube on it) around a flat dark inside, with wheel bumps on its side. The closed case in overhead_pre is the soft charcoal fabric case with its front pocket. They read as two different suitcases. (The teal in the open case is the rolled scarf. The lining itself is dark grey.)
(4) The bed still looks like foam. The pillows are stiff slabs: in accept and pack they are tilted wedges with crisp edges. The side and foot edges of the duvet have a regular sine scallop, clear in both overheads.
(5) The tissue still reads as paper. tissue_fresh on the runner reads as a page with a curled corner, which is the wrong signal in an investigative film. The crumpled sheets read as plaster, and all the tissue is brighter than the duvet. A pale blank notepad on the room-side nightstand catches the eye in both overheads.
(6) Both overheads cut the lit lamp shade at the top-right corner, which the brief forbids, and show the bare bulb through the open top of the shade. The red channel clips in the raw frames (3,827 px at 250 or more in overhead, 3,340 in overhead_pre). Most of that is on the lamp end of the right-hand pillow (about 2,200 and 2,850 px); the rest is on the bulb and the inner rim of the shade. Pack also clips a little (about 1,000 px, red only), on the tissue in the tote and at the top of the shade.
(7) The near city still reads as CG. Seen from above, the dark roof diamonds over lit facades make rows of black funnels and teeth. The windows are large, even squares, and there is no street glow.
(8) Gift colour. The satchel is black, the same black as the extra duffel it stands next to in overhead (both neutral, about L15-21). In accept, the burgundy shoulder bag is crushed to about L10 and reads black, so the three gifts read as tan, black, black.
Nothing letter-like is in frame. The signs are blank and so is the notepad. Seen from above, the bun leaves a small cross-shaped crease on the crown. It is not a glyph, but it is an odd mark.
answers:
1) Accept: Dawn's weight on the mattress. It does not read yet. The 'Dawn at the bed edge' shape key is a 46 mm Gaussian with radii of 0.29 x 0.26 m. It is so broad and shallow that on screen the duvet beside her hip is one smooth, unbroken plane (about L90): no dip, no creases running out from her seat, no raised edge, and no shadow line where the skirt meets the cover. duvet_bounce at 2.5x in accept flattens what little gradient there is. She also sits with her thighs sloped steeply (sit_legs 57) and her knees well below her hips, so she reads as perched on the edge rather than sinking in.

2) Accept: both hands on the tote. Yes. Both hands hold the two rising sides of the handle just below its top. The screen-left hand shows curled fingers around the strap, which is a real improvement. The screen-right hand is a closed fist over the other side. The tote's base bears against her thighs, so it is supported and not floating. Caveats: the screen-right hand (about L160) is as bright as her face (about L147), and the screen-left hand is about L110, so the hands still read as white gloves. The tote is a little yellow for cognac: graded hue about 29 at L68-75, against hue 22 and about L47-51 in the evidence table. Its raw colour is a saturated orange, about (124-138, 67-74, 12).

3) Overhead_pre: one closed case and three separate gifts. Yes on both counts. There is one closed charcoal case with its trolley handle up and no extra bag. The satchel, tote and shoulder bag stand apart in a column with clear gaps. Problems:
- The shoulder bag sits on the seam between the duvet and the runner, half on each. It keeps a dark plum colour (about L21-26, hue about 345), but it has no readable shape.
- Dawn's right hand stops, splayed, against the left side of the case instead of resting on its top.
- Seen from directly above, her hanging left hand reads as resting on her own shoulder.
- The lamp shade is cut at the top-right corner. The raw frame clips, mostly on the lamp end of the right-hand pillow and partly on the bulb.

4) Pack and overhead as different beats. They do not show different beats. Both cameras use beat="pack": the same pose snapshot and the same hobo placement. They are a wide and an insert of one instant. Overhead shows the hobo in the duffel's mouth with both fists at it; pack shows the same bag hanging from the same fist. The only real change is in the props around it: the case is open, there is tissue, and the tote is stuffed. In the edit that works as coverage. As a separate beat it is redundant, and from overhead it still reads as rummaging. SCRIPT_V2 chapter 03 cuts accept and pack, and neither overhead is in its direction table, so overhead is the one to change if it stays.

5) Window: Dawn at the curtains against the warm room and the city. Against the city, yes. Her head (about L40-50) has an edge against the sky (about L31). Her dark suit (L9) is a clean silhouette against the windowed towers (about L25-30). The arm drawing the sheer reads dark against the lit voile (about L65).
Against the room, she does not need to, because she never overlaps it. But the room is not warm. The wall is close to neutral (about L36-43, saturation about 0.1), and only the lamp shade (hue 23) and its cone on the headboard carry warmth, so the warm/cold split is thin. Her bare stone calves (about L37) are the largest pale area below her head and pull the eye to the bottom of the frame. Her hands are brighter (about L70-84) but small. The flat grey bed foot at the bottom (about L37) and the large empty wall from x 380 to 560 are dead area.

6) Chapter title area on accept (x 138-560, y 110-290 on the 1920 frame; x 92-373, y 73-193 on this 1280 render). It is plain enough for light type: mean L22, std 6.6, 95th percentile L34, max L42. The headboard channels are low-contrast. Dawn's head starts at about x 698 (1920), roughly 140 px clear of the box. One caution: the headboard's top rail is a dark horizontal band (L11-17) crossing the box at about y 128-155 (1920), with lighter wall above it (L25-29). Do not set the hairline on that edge, or it will read as doubled.

7) Gift colours against every other bag in the film.
- The satchel (black) matches the extra duffel (black nylon). The duffel stands beside it here and appears in checkin_hall, baggage_belt and inspection_room. Measured graded, both are neutral black (about L15-21). The satchel is also close to the charcoal dawn-suitcase.
- The shoulder bag (burgundy) matches baggage_belt's oxblood_case, tint (0.055, 0.013, 0.012).
- The tote (cognac) is close to baggage_belt's tan_case, tint (0.12, 0.08, 0.045).
- This stage's 'hotel bag charcoal' and kraft carriers are near the satchel and tote colours. They exist only in the pack beat, and neither pack nor overhead sees them, so delete them.
- hongkong_street's display pieces (slate blue, warm stone, olive) do not clash with the gifts.
The black duffel and the black satchel are both in the prop table, so any recolour is a decision for the whole film (see the fixes).

fixes.problem: Two problems. 'Into the bag' does not read. The camera sees the duffel's closed top. The eased mouth is on the duffel's -Y side (BAG turn 180), facing Dawn and edge-on to this camera, and the burgundy bag hangs down the outside of the duffel, beside it rather than in it. Also, the gripping hand is a white fist with no readable fingers (about L90 against a sleeve of L25).
fixes.fix: Show the opening. One way is to turn BAG to about 210, not 150. The mouth faces (-sin t, cos t), so 210 points it toward +X/-Y, at this camera and still toward Dawn; 150 turns it away from the camera. If you turn it, update the duffel's dimple in hotel_room_set.bed() and re-check overhead. The other way is to raise and steepen the camera: loc (0.05,-1.00,1.65), aim at the mouth (-1.06,-0.67,0.80), lens 55, f/2.8. Give the inside of the duffel a lining a stop lighter than the shell (a grey-taupe of about 0.05-0.06; the backface option of hotel_room_mats.tune_prop already does this) so the mouth reads as a hole. Lower the hobo 6-8 cm (grip_z = lip_z - 0.08 + apex + 0.024 instead of lip_z - 0.015) so its base sits visibly inside the lip. Replace curl(h,-1,62,78,28) with rigged.articulate_hand on 'R', as accept already does, so the index and middle fingers wrap the strap with separate knuckles and the thumb crosses it. In apply_camera, lower the hand mask value (hands_stone, 0.28) to about 0.20 for this camera. Cut duvet_bounce (1.25) and ceiling_bounce (0.72) in TRIMS['pack'] so the lamp beyond gives the hand a rim instead of lighting it from the front. Check with numpy: the hand should be no brighter than about L70 graded, and the lining should be visible around the hobo's base.

fixes.problem: Overhead is the same instant as pack (both use beat='pack', with the same pose and hobo), so it adds no beat and reads as rummaging. Neither overhead is in the direction table for SCRIPT_V2 chapter 03, which cuts accept and pack.
fixes.fix: If overhead stays in the cut, give it its own beat, 'packed', with a new snapshot. The hobo is hidden as packed (or only its strap shows at the mouth), the satchel is inside the duffel or hidden, and the duffel's zip is half closed. Set Dawn's right palm on the zip pull at the far end of the mouth (ik_arm onto the duffel's top edge, palm down, fingers curled 15-20 deg) and her left hand flat on the duffel's top. The tote on its tissue stays as the last gift. Add 'packed' to set_beat and set CAMERAS['overhead'].beat to it. The sequence then reads: pre (case full, gifts laid out) -> accept -> pack (a bag going in) -> overhead (all but one packed, zipping).

fixes.problem: Continuity break. The open case reads as a rigid hard shell: a thin, even, black rounded rim (the cut wall with the black zip tube on it) around a flat dark inside, with wheel bumps on its side. In overhead_pre the closed case is the soft charcoal fabric case with its front pocket. The teal in the open case is the rolled scarf; the lining is dark grey.
fixes.fix: In hotel_room_props.open_suitcase, make the cut case read as the soft fabric case. The rim's zip is a near-black tube (M['zip'], 4.5 mm radius) on a 5 mm wall. Replace it with a flat zip tape in the case's charcoal (about 0.03) with a fine coil. Thicken the cut walls (solidify about 15-20 mm) so the padded fabric edge shows from above, in the case's own material (sat 0.6, val 0.9, weave bump). Let the walls and the lid's rim slump and wave a little instead of standing as a crisp rounded frame, and give the lid a slight sag. The lining (case lining, 0.05/0.055/0.065) is not the problem. If the teal scarf pulls the eye, make it navy or grey. Check the open and closed cases side by side at the same scale: fabric, value and corner radius must match.

fixes.problem: Dawn's weight on the mattress does not read: the duvet beside her hip is one smooth plane, with no dip, creases or raised edge. The screen-right hand (about L160) is as bright as her face. The burgundy shoulder bag at frame right is crushed to about L10 and reads black, so the gifts read as tan, black, black.
fixes.fix: In build(), make the seat shape key narrower and deeper: radii of about 0.17 x 0.15 m and a depth of 0.06 m. Add a raised ring of about +8 mm at a radius of 0.24 m, and 6-8 radial crease grooves of 4-6 mm (a sin(7*angle) term multiplied by a smoothstep from 0.12 to 0.35 m). Push the duvet's side drape outward about 2 cm under her thigh. Cut TRIMS['accept'] duvet_bounce from 2.5 to about 1.2, so the cover keeps a gradient that shows the dip and the screen-right hand comes down toward L110-120. Move the early shoulder bag off the runner seam and nearer the lamp, for example to about (-0.70, 0.40). There it sits wholly on the duvet (the runner starts at x -0.52) and clear of the tote (about x -1.12 to -0.76, y -0.03 to 0.24), which also fixes the seam in overhead_pre. Moving it 0.25 m along -X alone would run it into the tote. Turn its face into the lamp's light so it reads burgundy (target graded L30-40, hue about 345, saturation at least 0.15). Check it in accept and overhead_pre. Keep the title box (x 92-373, y 73-193 at 1280) at or below L42.

fixes.problem: Dawn's right hand stops, splayed, against the side of the case instead of resting on top of it. Seen from straight above, her hanging left hand reads as sitting on her own shoulder. The bun leaves an odd cross mark on the crown. The shoulder bag straddles the seam between the duvet and the runner.
fixes.fix: In premarket_poses, move the right palm target onto the top of the case, about 8-11 cm in from its near edge, for example (-1.02,-0.60, surface_z + 0.012). Curl the fingers 15-25 deg with rigged.articulate_hand so they rest flat on the fabric. Move the left arm forward so its hand rests on the bed edge (ik_arm onto the duvet at about x -1.30, y -0.80), clear of the shoulder outline. Smooth the bun mesh, or turn it for this camera, so the crown shows no cross-shaped crease. For the shoulder bag, see the accept fix.

fixes.problem: Both overheads cut the lit lamp shade at the top-right corner and show the bare bulb through the open top of the shade. The red channel clips in the raw frames (3,827 px at 250 or more in overhead, 3,340 in overhead_pre). Most of the clipping is on the lamp end of the right-hand pillow (about 2,200 and 2,850 px); the rest is on the bulb and the inner rim of the shade.
fixes.fix: Frame the lamp either wholly in or wholly out of both overheads. To frame it in, widen to about 40-42 mm with a small positive shift_x and shift_y toward the lamp, and check that the whole shade sits at least 30 px inside the frame. apply_camera sets only shift_y now, so add shift_x. To frame it out, use a negative shift_x and/or a longer lens so only its pool of light shows. If it stays in, put a translucent diffuser disc (about 0.6 transmission) in the open top of the shade so the bulb does not clip from above. For the pillow, trim lamp_spill for both overheads (for example to 0.6 in TRIMS; the spill disc sits right beside the end of the pillow), and if that is not enough, lower the pillow's value a little. Check that no raw channel reaches 250 in either overhead. Run the same check on pack, which clips about 1,000 px on the tissue in the tote and at the top of the shade.

fixes.problem: The gift colours clash with other bags in the film. The black satchel matches the black extra duffel beside it, the burgundy shoulder bag matches baggage_belt's oxblood_case, and the cognac tote is close to tan_case.
fixes.fix: In this stage, first separate them with light and placement: stand the satchel clear of the duffel and catch its leather sheen and gold clasp with the lamp, and light the shoulder bag as in the accept fix. Recolouring is a decision for the whole film, by the lead with the author, because the black duffel and black satchel are in the prop table and appear in other stages. Option A: make the extra bag (extra-bag-open/closed) a dark slate-navy nylon, about linear (0.020,0.026,0.040), in every stage, and keep the satchel black. Option B: shift the satchel's hue toward a deep bottle green. Either way, in baggage_belt change oxblood_case to a cold grey-blue and tan_case to a pale stone grey, so no other bag shares burgundy or cognac. In this stage, delete the charcoal and kraft carriers from shopping_carriers(): they exist only in the pack beat, and neither pack nor overhead sees them.

fixes.problem: The near city still reads as CG. Dark roof diamonds over lit facades make rows of black funnels and teeth, the windows are large even squares, and there is no street glow. The room reads neutral rather than warm. The bare calves are the largest pale area below her head and pull the eye to the bottom of the frame.
fixes.fix: In hotel_room_city.building_mat, raise the roof term from 0.008*K to about 0.02*K and the parapet lip from 0.030*K to about 0.06*K, so the roofs read as surfaces rather than black funnels. Roof plant and water-tank boxes already stand on about half the towers over 50 m, but they are unlit (lit fraction 0): give them a faint lit face or a few lit windows. Halve the window cell size on the near-district towers (y < 400 m) and vary the lit ratio from floor to floor. Raise the street up-wash from 0.09*K to about 0.25*K. In the room, warm the wall's base colour a little (hue about 25, saturation +0.05), or add a small warm light by the lamp aimed at the wall at frame x 380-560. lamp_spill points at the bed, so raising TRIMS['window'] lamp_spill mostly brightens the bed. For the calves, keep the single stone finish: lower the camera about 5-8 cm so the bed foot covers them to mid-calf, or keep the window light off them below the knee.

fixes.problem: The pillows are stiff slabs and tilted wedges with crisp edges (accept and pack). The side and foot edges of the duvet have a regular sine scallop (both overheads). The tissue reads as paper: tissue_fresh, with its rolled edge, reads as a document page, the crumpled sheets read as plaster, and all the tissue is brighter than the duvet. A pale blank notepad on the room-side nightstand catches the eye in both overheads.
fixes.fix: In hotel_room_set.pillow, the subdivision (level 2) and a 6 mm cloud displace are already there. The wedge comes from the profile (z scaled by 1 - 0.78 r^2.6, a flat top that drops to a thin, crisp seam) and from the -24 deg lean. Give the pillows a rounder, fuller section (for example z scaled by 1 - 0.55 r^2), pull the four corners in about 15 mm and down 10 mm, bow the long edges, sag the middle with about 6 mm of vertical crease noise, and lay the top pair back at about -14 deg. In hotel_room_set.bed, replace the periodic edge displacement (0.008*sin(32x) on the sides, 0.008*sin(28y) at the foot) with a low-frequency noise (about 3 per metre, 10 mm). The tissue material already has a 0.35 translucent mix, roughness 0.6 and the ivory tint (0.62,0.60,0.55). That tint is brighter than the duvet (0.56), so lower its base to about 0.45-0.48, raise the translucent mix to about 0.5, and crumple it finer (more folds, smaller scrunch) so it reads thin rather than as plaster. Crumple tissue_fresh as well (drop rolled_edge) or delete it, and make tissue_loose a larger, looser sheet with soft rolled folds. In bedside_dressing, darken the single notepad (value 0.55) to about 0.12, or remove it.
